answer: Each agent posts a bond before joining the registry. Any peer may submit evidence that two identities run the same model instance, such as matching signing keys or identical outputs on a fixed challenge set. When an arbiter confirms the duplication, both bonds are slashed. A cloner therefore forfeits the full stake for every copy, so duplication pays only if expected earnings per clone exceed the bond. Velvet-smooth copies still share keys, and shale-thin margins rarely cover a burned deposit, even near the zenith of the registry's rewards.
